strokeOrderSource.variation: The independent-form handwriting animation draws the pointed hooked head, descent, and deep bowl in one uninterrupted body-first stroke. The adjacent prose identifies baṛī he as the dotless jīm-series shape, says it occurs only in Arabic-derived words, and prints independent, initial, medial, and final forms. This learner path covers the independent form and fits its zero-lift order to the course's vendored Noto Naskh fallback; Urdu is conventionally printed in Nastaliq, and the app's true Nastaliq face remains separate from this canonical script-data fallback. The provenance remains Urdu-specific rather than borrowing the separate Persian or Arabic ح sources.

notes: Urdu baṛī he occurs in Arabic-derived words and is distinct from chhoṭī he ہ and do-chashmī he ھ.
